From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: evelyn.hart@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 15:15:00 -0700
Subject: March KPI packet + QBR prep: action items & follow-ups

Team — attaching the March KPI packet for leadership review ahead of this week's QBR prep slot. Highlights to scan first: p50/p95 token latency (hosted & dedicated), cost per 1k tokens trends, uptime SLO compliance, and active usage by top 10 customers.

Quick callouts: 
- Latency: hosted p95 is up ~40ms month-over-month; regional spike in EU appears concentrated on long-tail requests. See latency_by_region.xlsx.
- Cost: overall cost/unit is down 6% vs Jan thanks to batching; some deviation in low-volume models.
- Uptime: 99.94% (downtime incident on 2/10 fully mitigated).
- Usage: GAU up 18% MoM driven by mid-market renewals.

Requests: 
1) Evelyn/Neha — can you validate the EU p95 regression and confirm root-cause hypothesis (prefetch/cache invalidation vs kernel scheduling)? Need short answer by Wed EOD.
2) Stephanie — lead a 1-hr cost deep-dive with infra ops to identify immediate 1-2 config changes we can ship before the QBR.
3) Jordan — prepare 2 slides showing customer impact (tokens, errors, SLA hits) for the QBR.

Attachments: 202602_kpi_dashboard.pdf (packet), latency_by_region.xlsx, cost_trends_q1.csv

Thanks — please mark action owners on the shared doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1QBR-packet-2026-March

-Marcus Lin
VP Product, Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: March KPI packet + QBR prep: action items & follow-ups

On Mon, 2 Mar 2026 at 15:15, Marcus Lin wrote:
> Team — attaching the March KPI packet for leadership review ahead of this week's QBR prep slot. Highlights to scan first: p50/p95 token latency (hosted & dedicated), cost per 1k tokens trends, uptime SLO compliance, and active usage by top 10 customers.
> 
> Quick callouts: 
> - Latency: hosted p95 is up ~40ms month-over-month; regional spike in EU appears concentrated on long-tail requests. See latency_by_region.xlsx.

Thanks Marcus — I pulled the EU slices and started a small trace analysis. Preliminary notes: 
- The p95 bump correlates with a subset of requests using long context windows (>8k). Those flows hit a different kernel path and we see heavier lock contention during high concurrency.
- There's a minor cache-invalid pattern after model-variant rollouts on 2/4 — KV caches warmed slowly for a small percentage of instances.

Actionable next steps I recommend: 
- Validate kernel scheduling patch in staging (I can own) and run via our continuous-batch harness by Wed morning.
- Add a short-term routing rule to prefer warmed instances for long-context requests until the kernel patch lands (risk: slightly higher cost).

I'll update the doc with specific experiment IDs and a short repro. Neha — can you confirm whether the rollout on 2/4 targeted EU-only infra or was global?

-Evelyn
Senior Director, Serving Runtime

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: March KPI packet + QBR prep: action items & follow-ups

Evelyn — confirmed: the variant rollout on 2/4 was global but initially pushed small cohorts in eu-west1 and europe-north. The canary window expanded; the majority of global instances received it by 2/5.

Notes from infra ops: 
- We saw ~2.1% of instances report cache warm failures (timing out on the prefetch job) during the rollout; those map to the EU spike in the telemetry slice.
- Ops has a quick mitigation: re-run the prefetch job and drain traffic from affected instances for 30m.

Jordan — per Marcus's ask, can you bake a single slide with: (a) impact on top 5 customers by tokens, (b) outage/incidents timeline, (c) proposed near-term mitigation and expected SLA delta?

-Neha
Director, Infrastructure
